methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $300K total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Hedral is a seed-stage company in Housing & Construction founded by Arjo Mozumder. The analysis draws on a peer set of five private-sector comparables (BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, Ground Control Development, ADMARES), with no public company benchmarks available in the sector.

The valuation employs a stage-progression methodology anchored to Hedral's $300K total raised as a proxy baseline value. Applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $750K. This method is applicable given the company's current seed funding position and the presence of relevant private peers.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $638K to $862K, with a median of $750K. The relatively narrow range reflects the single-method approach and reflects uncertainty inherent in early-stage valuation. Key limitations include the absence of public comparables to benchmark against sector multiples, limited visibility into Hedral's operational metrics (revenue, users, growth rate), and reliance on a single progression-based method. The analysis would benefit from additional data on peer funding rounds, burn rates, and market traction to refine the range and improve confidence in the midpoint estimate.
